issues.legal_issue: A limitation period in a separate statute does not govern an application under a statute that prescribes no limitation period, where that statute does not adopt the separate statute and the Limitation Act does not apply.
material_facts: A tenant applied under the governing tenancy statute for possession of agricultural land.
The governing statute prescribed no limitation period for that application, and the Limitation Act did not apply to the proceeding.
The application was dismissed as time-barred solely by applying a limitation period found in a different tenancy statute.
The governing statute contained no provision making the other statute applicable to proceedings under it.
issues.conclusion: The application was not barred by limitation; the decisions dismissing it on that ground were set aside, and the matter was remanded for a decision on its merits.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 43 of the Pepsu Tenancy and Agricultural Lands Act, 1955, no limitation period applied because that Act prescribed none and the Limitation Act did not apply. Section 50 of the Punjab Tenancy Act, 1887, could not be incorporated into proceedings under the Pepsu Act in the absence of a provision in the Pepsu Act making the Punjab Act applicable. The Court relied on no earlier cases.

rule.if: application_under_silent_statute and statute_does_not_adopt_separate_limitation_rule and limitation_framework_does_not_apply and dismissed_as_time_barred

predicates.application_under_silent_statute: A person filed an application under a statute that does not prescribe a limitation period for that application.
predicates.statute_does_not_adopt_separate_limitati: The statute governing the application does not make a limitation rule in a separate statute applicable to the proceeding.
predicates.limitation_framework_does_not_apply: The generally applicable limitation framework does not apply to the proceeding.
predicates.dismissed_as_time_barred: The decision-maker dismissed the application as time-barred by applying a limitation rule from a separate statute.

issues.definition: When an application under a statute with no prescribed limitation period is dismissed as time-barred, the application is not barred by limitation if the statute does not adopt a separate limitation rule and the general limitation framework does not apply.
